title: Session triage & weighting — brain dump
content:
NOTE: quick personal scratchpad. Goal = capture heuristics and low-friction experiments for session-level priority weighting so we can carve predictable capacity and improve cost/latency trade-offs for paid vs free tiers. Not a polished PRD; more like a set of riffs + minimal rollout plan.

Problem statement
- We have mixed traffic: free users (burst, noisy), paid customers with SLAs, and background batch jobs. With finite Dedicated pools we need an online way to rank/triage sessions so high-value work gets better latency and lower preemption.
- Current routing is coarse: customer-tier -> model -> region. No fine-grained session priority. Results: tail latency spikes under load, noisy tenants affect cost and QoE.

Goal / success metrics (initial)
- Reduce 95th token-latency for SLA customers by 20% under 80% pool utilization.
- Keep overall token-cost increase <= 5% (we expect some overhead for prioritization).
- Maintain fairness: no single free user should have latency > 5x baseline for more than 1% of requests.

Core idea (sketch)
- Assign every incoming session a real-valued priority score P in [0,1] at request arrival. Routing and scheduling will use P to influence queue position and allocation of dedicated shards/burst capacity.
- P is a weighted aggregate of signals: customer_tier, SLA_flag, recent_payment_activity, session_activity_rate, predicted_response_time (model->tokens), historical-error-rate, and business_priority_tags (e.g., "enterprise-workflow").

Example scoring formula (toy):
P = clamp( w1 * tier_score + w2 * sla_flag + w3 * recency + w4 * 1/(1+pred_len) + w5 * affinity_score , 0, 1 )
where tier_score = {enterprise:1, paid:0.7, freemium:0.3, anon:0.0}, sla_flag = {true:1, false:0}, recency = exp(-age_hours/24) for last activity, pred_len = expected tokens remaining, affinity_score = fraction of requests routed to same customer shard historically (reward stickiness).

Heuristics and knobs
- Hard vs soft priorities: hard pinning for enterprise SLA sessions (no preemption), soft weights for paid vs free. Soft weights allow graceful slowdown (e.g., lower batching, additive latency).
- Decay window: recency weight should decay over minutes to avoid sticky high priority after one event.
- Budget caps: per-customer/overall priority budget to prevent a single customer from consuming all high-priority slots.
- Fallbacks: if capacity constrained, route low-P sessions to quantized/cheaper model variants or to a delayed queue with hints to client.

Operational model / scheduler tie-ins
- Scheduling layer will accept P and implement: (1) admission control (drop/queue), (2) queue ordering, (3) selective preemption, (4) model-variant routing.
- Quick implementation path: start with weighted FIFO (priority queue) at front-end LB per pool. No changes to runtime kernels initially.

User stories
- As a paid product manager, I want my customers' interactive calls to be prioritized so conversion-critical flows are snappy. Acceptance: 95th latency drops near expected.
- As an infra SRE, I want the system to surface which sessions are being throttled so we can trace regressions. Acceptance: logs + traces show P and outcome for 99% of calls.
- As a frontend engineer, I want a simple client flag to mark "background-sync" so those calls can be deprioritized automatically. Acceptance: client flag respected and visible in dashboards.

Experiment matrix (MVP):
- Experiment A: binary priority tiers (high/low) based on customer_tier + SLA_flag. Measure latency and cost.
- Experiment B: continuous scoring (formula above) with w's tuned via grid search on historical traffic. Compare to A.
- Experiment C: add model-variant fallback for low-P sessions and measure quality degradation (human eval on n=200 prompts).

Data required
- Historical request traces for 30d: tokens_in, tokens_out, latency, customer_id, session_id, model, estimated_remaining_tokens (approx), outcome codes.
- Billing/plan table to map customer tier/SLA.
- Small labeled set mapping a few session types -> business_priority to seed affinity_score.

Monitoring / dashboards
- New per-pool chart: P distribution over time. Heatmap of P vs observed latency percentiles.
- Alerts: sudden shift in P distribution (more low-P traffic suggests noisy adoption) or uptick in preempted requests.
- Tracing: include P and weight contributions in trace tags.

Rollout plan (conservative)
1) Simulate scoring offline on 30d traces; produce expected allocation and latency estimates.
2) Flag-only rollout: compute P and emit to logs without changing routing for 1 week. Verify distribution and customer impact.
3) Canary pool: enable weighted FIFO for 5% of traffic (non-enterprise) and run A/B. Monitor metrics.
4) Gradual ramp with budget caps and kill-switch.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Where to compute P? Edge LB vs control plane vs runtime? Latency suggests edge LB but that leaks business signals to public LB layer. Control plane adds extra hop. Tradeoff note: start in edge LB but ensure signals are obfuscated/hashed.
- Privacy: affinity_score uses historical routing; need to ensure this doesn't expose PII. Keep only aggregated counts.
- Gaming: free users might try to game recency or flags — need decay and budget checks.
- Complexity vs observability: continuous P is powerful but harder to explain to customers. Might need to expose only tiered labels in SLA docs.

Short-term TODOs (my personal list)
- [ ] Pull 30d traces and write sampling SQL (ask Data infra for export). Draft: SELECT customer_id, session_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, timestamp FROM requests WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '30 days';
- [ ] Prototype scoring script in Python notebook (use sample of 500k requests).
- [ ] Create Linear card for canary (linked above).
- [ ] Quick dashboard mock: P distribution + 95th latency by tier.

Notes to self
- Keep initial P space small: try two or three weights only (tier, sla, pred_len). Add others after we validate.
- Don't over-index on affinity early — it's noisy and will produce stickiness edge cases.
- Consider adding a "defer-until" field for background tasks (schedule window) instead of only deprioritizing.

References / related threads
- Past notes on "adaptive-fallbacks-brain-dump" and "session-priority-prd-draft" — reuse heuristics but try continuous scoring instead of binary tiers.
- Slack: #runtime-routing (search thread "priority pilot").

End of dump. Will refine into a short PRD if this looks reasonable.

-- Sana
